ov: About 26 species of long, silvery predatory fish with fang-like teeth and an underbite, found in tropical and subtropical oceans worldwide, near the surface, coral reefs and seagrass. They ambush prey with short bursts of speed and often bite smaller fish in half.

why.dg: Bites on swimmers are rare and are thought to happen in poor visibility or when a barracuda mistakes shiny jewellery for prey.
why.et: A popular food and game fish, usually eaten as fillets or steaks, though big ones can cause ciguatera poisoning.

len: Great barracuda: usually 60–100 cm; exceptionally over 1.5 m
rg: Tropical and subtropical oceans worldwide, including the Atlantic, Caribbean, Red Sea and Pacific.
df: Fish such as jacks, grunts, groupers, small tunas, mullets, herrings and anchovies.
fx: Larger barracudas have been linked to ciguatera fish poisoning when eaten.
Adults mostly hunt alone, while young and half-grown fish often gather in groups.
